subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Write the equation √3x + y + 10 = 0 in (a) slope-intercept form, (b) intercept form and (c) normal form.

mark_split.label: Divide and read cos α, sin α
Name α and write the normal form

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), book p.158, chapter 3 THE STRAIGHT LINE, Long Answer question 16(vi). **Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work** — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints a chapter-level marks banner over this section but no per-step allocation on any answer. The split follows the three parts the question names: two marks for each of the two easy forms, and four for the normal form, which is the only part with a sign condition in it — one for making the right side positive, two for dividing and reading cos α and sin α, and one for naming α. This book prints almost no exam-appearance years, so appearances[] is empty — the chapter has long been examined, we simply have no sourced years for this question. Paper position: Maths-1B Section C prints 3 long answer questions at 8 marks each and the student answers any 2, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Every form was checked back against the original. The slope-intercept form y = −√3x − 10 rearranges to √3x + y + 10 = 0; the intercept form x/(−10/√3) + y/(−10) = 1 multiplies out to √3x + y = −10; and the normal form, with cos 210° = −√3/2 and sin 210° = −1/2, reads −√3x/2 − y/2 = 5, which multiplies by −2 back to √3x + y = −10. The value p = 5 also agrees with the direct perpendicular distance from the origin, |0 + 0 + 10|/√((√3)² + 1²) = 10/2 = 5. LINES EXPANDED 2026-09-14 (founder direction, modelled on the Maths-2A, Maths-2B and Maths-1A expansions): every move is written on its own line, with the reason or the arithmetic shown before it is used; the steps, marks and split are unchanged.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this — name all three forms, and say what condition fixes the angle in the normal form.

steps.label: Slope-intercept form
steps.margin_note: The first two marks. Quote y = mx + c, make y the subject, and then read off m and c separately.
lines: (a) Slope-intercept form is  y = mx + c

recall.must_convey: That making y the subject gives y = −√3x − 10, so m = −√3 and c = −10.
accept: make y the subject to get y equals minus root three x minus ten
slope intercept form is y equals m x plus c
the slope is minus root three and c is minus ten
y ni subject ga cheste minus root three x minus ten vasthundi
m equals minus root three and c equals minus ten
heard_as: y equals m x plus c

steps.why: Slope-intercept form shows the slope and the y-intercept directly, so the work is to make y the subject.
steps.memory_tip: y = mx + c: make y the subject, then m is the number in front of x and c is what is left.

steps.label: Intercept form
steps.margin_note: The next two marks. Quote x/a + y/b = 1, move the constant to the right, and divide every term by it.

lines.text: (divide every term by −10, so that the right side is 1)

recall.must_convey: That dividing by −10 gives x/(−10/√3) + y/(−10) = 1.
accept: move the constant right and divide by minus ten
intercept form is x over a plus y over b equals one
a is minus ten over root three and b is minus ten
constant tho divide chesthe intercept form vasthundi
x over minus ten by root three plus y over minus ten equals one

steps.why: Intercept form must have 1 on the right-hand side, and dividing by the constant arranges that.
common_mistakes: Leaving the x term as √3x/(−10) instead of x over a single number.
Writing a as −10 and b as −10/√3, swapping the two.
steps.memory_tip: x/a + y/b = 1 needs 1 on the right, so divide by the constant and then move the √3 into the denominator.

steps.label: Make the right side positive
steps.margin_note: One mark. Normal form carries the condition p > 0. Move the constant across and, if it is negative, change every sign.

lines.text: (p is the length of the perpendicular from

lines: (c) Normal form is  x cos α + y sin α = p,

lines.text: (the right side −10 is negative; multiply every term by −1)

lines: √3x + y = −10 gives a negative right side,

recall.must_convey: That p must be positive, so the signs are changed to give −√3x − y = 10.
accept: normal form needs p positive so change every sign
minus root three x minus y equals ten
p is a distance so it cannot be negative
p positive undaali so signs anni marchali
make the right hand side positive first

steps.why: In normal form p is a perpendicular distance from the origin, so it must be positive, and that single condition is what fixes α.
common_mistakes: Dividing by 2 while the right side is still negative.
Changing the sign of only the constant term.
steps.memory_tip: p is a distance, so p > 0. If the constant is negative, change every sign at once.
lines_compact: (c) Normal form is  x cos α + y sin α = p,
√3x + y = −10 gives a negative right side,

steps.label: Divide and read cos α, sin α
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Divide every term by √((−√3)² + (−1)²) = 2, then read cos α, sin α and p off the result in that order.

lines.text: (divide by the square root of the sum of the squares
of the coefficients of x and y)
(compare with x cos α + y sin α = p)

recall.must_convey: That dividing by 2 gives cos α = −√3/2, sin α = −1/2 and p = 5.
accept: divide by two which is the root of three plus one
cos alpha is minus root three by two and sin alpha is minus half
p is five
root a square plus b square tho divide cheyyali
root of three plus one is two

steps.why: Dividing by the square root of the sum of the squares of the x and y coefficients makes them a cosine and a sine, because their squares then add to 1.
common_mistakes: Dividing the left side by 2 but leaving 10 on the right.
steps.memory_tip: √((√3)² + 1²) = √4 = 2, so this one divides by a whole number.

steps.label: Name α and write the normal form
steps.margin_note: The last mark. Use the signs of cos α and sin α to name the quadrant, then write the finished normal form with the angle in it.
lines: cos α and sin α are both negative, so α lies

lines.text: quadrant α = 180° + the related acute angle)

recall.must_convey: That both being negative puts α in the third quadrant, so α = 210°.
accept: both are negative so alpha is in the third quadrant
alpha is two hundred and ten degrees
x cos two ten plus y sin two ten equals five
rendu negative so third quadrant, alpha two ten
one eighty plus thirty gives two ten

steps.why: The signs of cos α and sin α together name one quadrant, and that is what turns the pair of values into a single angle α.
common_mistakes: Naming α as 30° from the size of the numbers, ignoring the two minus signs.
Using 60° as the related angle, from cos α = −√3/2 read as a sine.
steps.memory_tip: Both cosine and sine negative means the third quadrant, so α = 180° + the related acute angle.
lines_compact: cos α and sin α are both negative, so α lies
